clue.text: Promotion in new café for Walton's "entertainment"

indicators.note: in places the promotion piece within the reworked letters
new signals that the letters of the word café are made over into a fresh order

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a promotion

explanation.surface: A publicity stunt in a newly opened café supplies the music for a Walton show.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks round 'entertainment' flag Walton's own label for the work, not a show in general.
explanation.definitionFit: Façade is William Walton's 1922 setting of Edith Sitwell's poems, billed as an entertainment.

clue.text: Function at court in Irish islands

indicators.note: in tells us the court abbreviation sits within the island group's name

parts.note: the Aran Islands lie off the west coast of Ireland

explanation.surface: Some ceremony at a court held on Ireland's western islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Arctan, the inverse tangent, is a trigonometric function in mathematics.

clue.text: Astronomical instrument disturbed basalt ore

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of the rock words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A stargazing device has knocked over a heap of volcanic rock.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrolabe is an old device for measuring the altitude of stars and planets.

clue.text: Topless scene — one pert model on location of Blow-up?

indicators.note: model as a verb means shape or remould, so the gathered letters are rearranged
topless means the word scene loses its top, its opening letter

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A risqué photo shoot with a cheeky topless model, in the spirit of the film Blow-Up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' trims SCENE to CENE; with I and PERT the letters are remodelled. Blow-up is the 1966 Antonioni film about a photographer, but here it means an explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: The epicentre is the point at the surface directly above where a quake or explosion begins.

clue.text: Quartet in erotic surroundings for Dvorak overture

indicators.note: surroundings means the sexual word wraps around the number four

parts.note: carnal means sensual or erotic
a quartet is four, the Roman numeral IV

explanation.surface: A string quartet plays in a racy setting for the start of a Dvořák piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Dvořák wrote the Carnival Overture, Op. 92, a lively concert piece.

clue.text: Against the trip — because of the height indicated?

parts.note: con, as in pros and cons, means against
a tour is a trip

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to an outing on account of the altitude involved.
explanation.definitionFit: On a map a contour line joins points of equal height, so it shows elevation.

clue.text: Pointer endlessly padding about river

indicators.note: padding means the shortened clue fills out the middle of the word for about

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about or concerning

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for a pointer loses its final letter

parts.note: a hint is a pointer or tip

explanation.surface: A gun dog pads endlessly up and down a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: A pointer here is a tip, not the gun dog the surface suggests; RE is the crossword's usual 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhine is a major European river flowing from the Alps to the North Sea.

clue.text: State I owned up to nothing

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for owned is read from the bottom

parts.note: had means owned
O is nought, nothing

explanation.surface: A confession: I admitted to nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'up' reverses HAD to DAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty United States, in the northwest.

clue.text: Tissue helps out daughter, Unity, upset

indicators.note: upset means the gathered letters are overturned into a new order

parts.note: aids means helps out
unity is the number one

explanation.surface: A tearful daughter is helped out after a family upset over unity.
explanation.definitionFit: Adenoids are a mass of lymphatic tissue at the back of the nose.

clue.text: Prokofiev's suite, Hyacinths Variations, cut first

indicators.note: variations means the remaining letters are varied into a new order
cut first means the flower word loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: A concert programme pairing Prokofiev with a set of flowery variations, trimmed at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut first' drops the H of HYACINTHS, leaving YACINTHS to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Prokofiev's Scythian Suite is an orchestral work drawn from his ballet about the ancient Scythians.

clue.text: Half-back catching silver works by Debussy

indicators.note: catching means the reversed half word grabs the silver symbol in its middle
back means the word for half is turned around

parts.note: semi means half
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A rugby half-back catches a ball while a Debussy piece plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-back' looks like a rugby position, but it splits into the word for half and a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Debussy composed two sets of piano Images and a set of orchestral Images.

clue.text: Strauss opera confusing me also

indicators.note: confusing means the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone baffled by a Strauss opera admits it confuses them too.
explanation.definitionFit: Salome is Richard Strauss's 1905 one-act opera after Oscar Wilde's play.

clue.text: Three rounds DJ having yet to arrange as part of 25

indicators.note: arrange means the gathered letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: each round is the ring-shaped letter O, three of them

explanation.surface: A disc jockey with three sets still to arrange part of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is the Choral symphony, Beethoven's Ninth, whose finale sets Schiller's ode.
explanation.definitionFit: Ode to Joy is the choral finale of Beethoven's Ninth Symphony.

clue.text: Knock to indicate availability

definitions.meaning: beer on ... is available to draw, so a ... signals that supply is at hand

explanation.definitionFit: A tap is both a gentle knock and a valve that makes a supply available.

clue.text: Brahms composition could be a Holst parody

indicators.note: could be means the letters can be reformed into something else

explanation.surface: A Brahms piece might turn out to be a send-up of Holst.
explanation.definitionFit: Brahms's Alto Rhapsody, Op. 53, sets Goethe for contralto, male chorus and orchestra.

clue.text: Spanish port arranged cigar sale

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the sale words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A cigar sale has been organised at a Spanish harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeciras is a port in southern Spain on the Bay of Gibraltar.

clue.text: Towards the end of the day, it's poured for tramp

definitions.text: Towards the end of the day, it's poured
definitions.meaning: an evening drink taken at sunset
in Australia a swagman who arrives at dusk for shelter

explanation.definitionFit: A sundowner is both an evening drink and an Australian vagrant who turns up at nightfall.

clue.text: New USA work with a Japanese film director

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A new American project with a Japanese director attached.
explanation.definitionFit: Akira Kurosawa directed Seven Samurai and Rashomon.

clue.text: Suggested address to Miss Harlow having single drink at opera

indicators.note: suggested means the words are hinted at by their sound rather than their spelling

parts.note: speaking to the film star Jean Harlow you might say you, Jean
single means one
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A man chats up Jean Harlow with a single gin at the opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene Onegin is Tchaikovsky's opera after Pushkin's verse novel.

clue.text: Arrest prohibition lifted

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition

explanation.surface: An arrest after a prohibition is lifted.
explanation.definitionFit: To nab someone is informal for to arrest them.

clue.text: Fancy thing that's worn in bed

definitions.text: Fancy thing that's worn in bed

indicators.note: fancy as a verb or adjective suggests the letters are freely rearranged

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A frilly item to wear in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the garment while also giving the wordplay; i.e. stands for 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress is a garment, often frilly, worn for sleeping.

clue.text: Distress signal for a castaway?

definitions.meaning: a firework rocket used as a warning or distress flare
a ... in old usage is someone abandoned on an island

explanation.definitionFit: Maroon names both a warning rocket and, archaically, one left stranded on a desert island.

clue.text: Top award given to composer for harpsichord variations

parts.note: gold is the first-place medal
Alban Berg was an Austrian composer

explanation.surface: A gold medal goes to a composer of harpsichord works.
explanation.definitionFit: Bach's Goldberg Variations are a set of thirty variations for harpsichord.

clue.text: The same extreme identity overturned

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue means both pieces together are read upwards

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means extreme
ID is short for identity

explanation.surface: The same extreme personality turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto means the same as stated before.

clue.text: Destroy Times leading editorial

parts.note: eras are times or ages

indicators.note: leading means just the front letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A demand to destroy the main editorial in The Times.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to wipe out or destroy.

clue.text: Church getting examination of Beethoven symphony

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A church is examining a Beethoven symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: The Choral Symphony is the nickname of Beethoven's Ninth.

clue.text: Flotow opera providing notes for Tam o'Shanter

indicators.note: providing means these letters together with the word notes would make up the poem's title

explanation.surface: A Flotow opera supplying the music for a Burns poem.
explanation.walkthrough: The opera's letters plus NOTES rearrange to TAM O'SHANTER, Burns's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Martha is Friedrich von Flotow's 1847 comic opera.

clue.text: Spiv returned, holding money for Puccini opera

indicators.note: holding means the reversed word clasps the currency in its middle
returned means the word for spiv is read backwards

parts.note: a tout is a spiv, someone hawking tickets
the rand is South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: A ticket spiv came back with money for a Puccini opera.
explanation.walkthrough: A spiv is British slang for a shady dealer; a ticket tout fits that description.
explanation.definitionFit: Turandot is Puccini's last opera, set in legendary China.

clue.text: Tea reduced during unsatisfactory opera

indicators.note: during means the shortened tea sits within the weak word

parts.note: lame means feeble or unsatisfactory

indicators.note: reduced means the tea's name loses its final letter

parts.note: bohea is a black China tea

explanation.surface: Tea is cut back during a disappointing night at the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: BOHEA is a China tea; 'reduced' trims it to BOHE, which goes 'during' LAME.
explanation.definitionFit: La Bohème is Puccini's opera about poor artists in Paris.
